purpose: Ground truth for the paraphrase debt gate. `same: true` means the gate SHOULD block b while a blocking debt on a is open. `same: false` means it MUST NOT.
howToUse: npm run calibrate:paraphrase — sweeps thresholds against a real embedder and prints the tradeoff. It recommends no number; a human picks one from the separation band.
unmetByNote: A pair may carry `unmetBy: [modelId]` when that specific model demonstrably cannot reach the correct answer. This keeps a known hole in the repo attached to the model that has it, instead of deleting the row (hiding it) or lowering the threshold to catch it (which drops below the number_swap band and starts refusing correct commits).

pairs.unmetWhy: Both sides Arabic. An English-only tokenizer reduces both to near-unknown tokens, so they may score high for the wrong reason — a coincidence, not comprehension. Recorded so a multilingual model has to earn this properly.

pairs.why: Both sides share a >256-token prefix and contradict only in the tail. scripts/embed_minilm.py truncates at 256 tokens, so these embed IDENTICALLY and score ~1.0 — the gate blocking on text it never read. No threshold fixes this; the fix is bounding or chunking claim_text at mint time. Present so calibration surfaces it instead of papering over it.
pairs.a: The operations manual defines the release process in full. Section one covers the change freeze, which begins seventy-two hours before any production deployment and applies to every service in the platform group without exception. Section two covers the approval chain: an engineer opens a change record, a second engineer reviews the diff, the on-call lead signs off, and the release manager schedules the window. Section three covers rollback, which must be demonstrated in staging before the change record can be approved, and which must complete within fifteen minutes of the decision to abort. Section four covers communication, including the customer notice template, the status page update, and the internal announcement that goes to the operations channel one hour before the window opens. Section five covers verification after the window closes, including the smoke suite, the error budget check, and the sign-off that closes the change record. Section six covers exceptions to all of the above, which require written approval from the director of engineering and are reviewed monthly. Section seven records that the retention period for release artefacts is ninety days.
